reservoir.title: Reservoir & Production Design — User Guide
reservoir.body:
Primary Fluid & Reservoir Parameters
Defines the hydrocarbon system and resource basis: primary fluid, in-place volume unit, PIIP, initial rate unit and value, play/zone, and world region.

What to enter: Oil or NG selection; valid unit selections; positive PIIP; positive per-well initial rate; play/zone; and region.

Used in the model: Normalizes the resource volume, establishes the principal production stream, selects the applicable context, and sets the initial production rate.

Review: Fluid and units must be internally consistent.

Production Forecast Parameters
Defines the decline curve and development geometry used to construct the type-well and field forecast.

What to enter: Type-well play ID A–G; hyperbolic b-factor; annual decline; exponential crossover year; terminal decline; target recovery factor; pool area; drainage length and width.

Used in the model: Builds the type-well production profile, estimates EUR, calculates drainage area and target wells, and scales production to the field.

Review: Enter ratios as decimals and dimensions in the displayed units.

Associated Fluids
Defines co-produced oil, gas, and water alongside the primary production stream.

What to enter: Associated oil ratio, associated gas ratio, initial water rate, and water growth factor.

Used in the model: Generates secondary production streams used in revenue and variable opex calculations.

Review: Use zero only when a stream is genuinely absent.

Wellbore and Completion Design
Defines the physical well design that drives drilling and completion capital.

What to enter: True vertical depth, lateral design/length, testing intervals, and testing/fracturing intervals.

Used in the model: Selects the applicable drilling-cost rates and applies completion costs per interval to each scheduled well.

Review: Interval counts are whole numbers and design should match the play.

schedule.title: Development Schedule — User Guide
schedule.body:
Year
Twenty-year project timing sequence for exploration, appraisal, facilities, development drilling, production, and cash flow.

What to enter: Use the fixed project-year sequence.

Used in the model: Provides the timing axis for capital spending, well additions, start-up, and production.

Review: Enter each activity in the intended project year.

Seismic Acquisition USD MM
Annual new seismic acquisition spending.

What to enter: USD millions; intended only for Years 1–3.

Used in the model: Creates early exploration and intangible capital in the selected years.

Review: Enter USD MM, not whole USD.

Seismic Reprocessing USD MM
Annual cost to reprocess existing seismic data.

What to enter: USD millions; intended only for Years 1–3.

Used in the model: Adds pre-development intangible capital.

Review: Use zero or blank when not applicable.

Exploration Wells
Exploration wells drilled by year.

What to enter: Whole-number well count.

Used in the model: Applies well design and cost assumptions to exploration activity timing.

Review: Do not enter fractional wells.

Appraisal Wells
Appraisal wells drilled by year.

What to enter: Whole-number well count.

Used in the model: Applies well design and cost assumptions to the appraisal program.

Review: Do not enter fractional wells.

Facilities Enter X
Marker identifying the facilities installation or commissioning year.

What to enter: Enter X in the chosen facilities year; normally use one marker.

Used in the model: Times facilities capital and helps establish the development start-up sequence.

Review: Align facilities timing with first production.

FFDP Producer Wells
Full-field development producer wells drilled by year.

What to enter: Whole-number producer-well count.

Used in the model: Builds the field production ramp and applies drilling/completion capital to each annual well tranche.

Review: The schedule should reconcile to the target well count.

costs.title: Drilling & Completion Costs — User Guide
costs.body:
Vertical drilling unit cost by depth
Cost curve for vertical drilling at TVD reference points from 1,500 m to 5,000 m.

What to enter: USD per metre at each depth point.

Used in the model: The engine selects or interpolates the appropriate vertical drilling rate for the entered TVD.

Review: Use region-appropriate market estimates.

Lateral drilling unit cost by length
Cost curve for lateral drilling at reference lengths from 1,000 m to 3,000 m.

What to enter: USD per metre at each lateral point.

Used in the model: Applies incremental lateral drilling cost when a lateral design is used.

Review: Confirm the lateral design in Step 1.

Perforating and testing cost
Cost for a non-fractured test or completion interval.

What to enter: USD per interval.

Used in the model: Multiplies the number of testing intervals by the unit cost.

Review: Enter a current unit cost.

Perforating, testing and fracturing cost
Cost for a fractured completion interval.

What to enter: USD per interval.

Used in the model: Multiplies fractured intervals by the unit cost.

Review: Avoid double-counting intervals.

Learning factor after 5 / 10 wells
Efficiency factors applied as the drilling campaign matures.

What to enter: Decimal cost factors; values below 1.0 represent cost reduction.

Used in the model: Reduces later-well drilling and completion costs based on cumulative activity.

Review: Use factors consistent with the expected learning curve.

facilities.title: Facilities Capex — User Guide
facilities.body:
4A | Gas Facilities
Capacity and capex benchmark tiers for gas developments.

What to enter: Annual design capacity in m³/year and capex in USD MM by component.

Used in the model: Selects or interpolates facilities requirements based on peak modeled gas production.

Review: Capacity tiers should cover the expected production range.

4B | Oil Facilities
Capacity and capex benchmark tiers for oil developments.

What to enter: Annual design capacity in bbl/year and capex in USD MM by component.

Used in the model: Selects or interpolates facilities requirements based on peak modeled oil production.

Review: Capacity tiers should increase consistently.

Design Capacity
Maximum annual throughput represented by each tier.

What to enter: m³/year for gas or bbl/year for oil.

Used in the model: Matches the modeled production requirement to an appropriate facilities scale.

Review: Use annual capacity, not daily capacity.

Primary Facility
Core processing or central production facility cost.

What to enter: USD MM by tier.

Used in the model: Forms the principal facilities capital component.

Review: Include the intended processing scope.

Associated Facilities
Supporting utilities and ancillary facilities cost.

What to enter: USD MM by tier.

Used in the model: Adds supporting infrastructure to total facilities capital.

Review: Use consistent scope across tiers.

Flow Lines
In-field gathering and flowline cost.

What to enter: USD MM by tier.

Used in the model: Adds field collection infrastructure.

Review: Align with field size and well count.

Export / Tie-in Pipeline
Cost to connect the field to export or existing infrastructure.

What to enter: USD MM by tier.

Used in the model: Adds export or tie-in infrastructure to total facilities capital.

Review: Reflect distance and connection complexity.

opex.title: Opex & Commodity Pricing — User Guide
opex.body:
Variable opex escalation
Annual multiplier on unit operating costs.

What to enter: Annual factor; 1.01 represents 1% annual escalation.

Used in the model: Escalates water, gas, and oil variable cost rates over time.

Review: Enter a factor, not a percentage display value.

Fixed opex escalation
Annual multiplier on fixed annual operating cost.

What to enter: Annual factor.

Used in the model: Escalates recurring fixed opex through project life.

Review: Use a consistent inflation basis.

Water / Gas / Oil variable opex
Unit cost of handling or producing each stream.

What to enter: USD/bbl water, USD/m³ gas, and USD/bbl oil.

Used in the model: Multiplies each annual production stream by its applicable cost rate.

Review: Use appropriate net operating costs.

Fixed opex
Base recurring annual field operating cost.

What to enter: USD/year.

Used in the model: Adds annual cost independent of production volume.

Review: Confirm the input is USD, not USD MM.

Gas / Oil sales price
Starting net realized commodity price.

What to enter: Positive numeric price in the displayed unit.

Used in the model: Applied to annual production before escalation and scenario multipliers.

Review: Use a common price-date basis.

Gas / Oil price escalation
Annual multiplier for the commodity price deck.

What to enter: 1.02 represents 2% annual escalation; 1.00 represents a flat price.

Used in the model: Builds the annual price deck from the initial value.

Review: Use a consistent nominal or real basis.

fiscal.title: Economics & Fiscal Controls — User Guide
fiscal.body:
Scenario Multipliers
Top-level controls for flexing capex, opex, production, and commodity prices.

What to enter: 1.00 = base case; 1.10 = 10% increase; 0.90 = 10% decrease.

Used in the model: Applies scenario adjustments without rebuilding the underlying detailed assumptions.

Review: Change one driver at a time for clear sensitivities.

Total capex / Total opex multiplier
Global adjustments to modeled capital or operating cost.

What to enter: Multiplier.

Used in the model: Scales all applicable capex or opex after the base calculation.

Review: Avoid double-counting detailed cost changes.

Oil / Gas / Water production multiplier
Global adjustment to each production stream.

What to enter: Multiplier by stream.

Used in the model: Scales annual production volumes and related variable costs.

Review: Use factors appropriate to the selected fluid case.

Oil / Condensate and Gas price multiplier
Global adjustment to the commodity price deck.

What to enter: Multiplier by commodity.

Used in the model: Scales the escalated prices used in annual revenue.

Review: Useful for downside and upside cases.

Fiscal Model Terms
Controls government/investor revenue allocation and the valuation basis.

What to enter: World region, PSA or CTR selector, and discount rate.

Used in the model: Applies the selected fiscal logic and discounts investor cash flows.

Review: Confirm the regime before interpreting results.

Fiscal model selector
Selects Production Sharing Agreement or Contract Tax/Royalty treatment.

What to enter: Text selection: PSA or CTR.

Used in the model: Determines how project revenue is divided between investor and government.

Review: Use the fiscal regime that matches the project.

Discount rate
Required return used for NPV.

What to enter: Decimal percentage; 0.15 represents 15%.

Used in the model: Discounts annual investor cash flows to the valuation date.

Review: Use a rate consistent with the case basis and risk.

Marker identifying the facilities installation or commissioning year.

What to enter: Enter X in the chosen facilities year; normally use one marker.

Used in the model: Times facilities capital and helps establish the development start-up sequence.

Review: Align facilities timing with first production.

state-rent@2.0.0-candidate.1:ui!p25.title: Producer wells drilled — Year 18
state-rent@2.0.0-candidate.1:ui!p25.body:
This input: Producer wells drilled — Year 18. Displayed unit: wells/year.

Full-field development producer wells drilled by year.

What to enter: Whole-number producer-well count.

Used in the model: Builds the field production ramp and applies drilling/completion capital to each annual well tranche.

Review: The schedule should reconcile to the target well count.

state-rent@2.0.0-candidate.1:ui!m26.title: Exploration wells drilled — Year 19

Exploration wells drilled by year.

What to enter: Whole-number well count.

Used in the model: Applies well design and cost assumptions to exploration activity timing.

Review: Do not enter fractional wells.
